title: मेचे जातिमा प्रचलित विवाह पद्धति {Marriage System Prevalent in the Meche Caste}
nepali: यो लेख मेचे जातिमा प्रचलित विवाह पद्धतिसँग सम्बन्धित विविध पक्षको विश्लेषणमा केन्द्रित छ । मेचे आदिवासी जनजाति समुदायअन्तर्गत पर्ने अल्पसंख्यक लोपोन्मुख जातीय समूह हो । नेपाल बाहिर भारतका भारतको आसाम, पश्चिम बंगाल, सिक्किम तथा भुटानका केही क्षेत्रहरूमा पनि यिनीहरू बसोबास गर्दछन्। नेपालमा भने यो जातिको बसोबास विशेषतः प्रदेश नं १ को झापा जिल्लाका जलथल, भद्रपुर नगरपािलका लखनपुर अनारमुनी, ज्यामिरगढी, बाहुनडाँगी, शनिश्चरे, चकचकी, भद्रपुर नगरपालिका, अनारमुनी, महेशपुर बनियानीजस्ता विभिन्न गाउँवस्तीहरूमा पाइन्छ । यिनीहरूका मौलिक सामाजिक, सांस्कृतिक, धार्मिक विशेषता यो आदिवासी जनजातिलाई चिनाउने प्रमुख आधार हुन्। त्यसमा पनि विवाह पद्धति र प्रकार यो जातिका पहिचानका सूत्र मानिन्छन्। अतः मेचे जातिमा प्रचलित विवाह पद्धतिलाई यस अध्ययनको विषय बनाइएको हो । यो अध्ययनमा प्राथमिक तथा द्वितीयक दुवै प्रकारका तथ्याङ्क एवम्सूचना सङ्कलन तथा विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । द्वितीयक तथ्याङ्क एवम्सूचना पूर्वकार्य समीक्षा र प्राथमिक तथ्याङ्क मूलतः झापा जिल्लाको धाइजन, मेचीनगर, बाहुनडाँगी, इटाभट्टा, अनारमनीजस्ता गाउँवस्तीमा बसोबासगर्ने मेचे समुदायबाट सङ्कलन गरिएको हो । विश्लेषणात्मक र विवरणात्मक ढाँचामा आधारित यो अध्ययनमा सङ्ख्यात्मकभन्दा गुणात्मक तथ्याङ्क प्रयोग गरिएका छन्।
american_english: This paper focuses on analyzing various aspects related to the marriage system prevalent in the Meche caste. The Meche community is an indigenous ethnic group under the Adivasi Janajati community and is a minority group facing extinction. Outside Nepal, they also live in some areas of India including Assam, West Bengal, Sikkim, and Bhutan. In Nepal, this caste is mainly found in various villages of Jalthal, Bhadrapur municipality in Jhapa district, such as Lakhanpur Anarmuni, Jamirmagarhi, Bauhundangi, Shanischare, Chakchaki, Bhadrapur municipality, Anarmuni, and Mahahpur Baniyani. Their unique social, cultural, and religious characteristics are the main elements that distinguish this indigenous community. The marriage system and its type are also considered as a symbol of identity for this caste. Therefore, the prevalent marriage system in the Meche caste has been made the subject of this study. This study has collected and analyzed both primary and secondary types of data and statistics. Secondary data and statistics were collected through literature review, while primary data were mainly collected from the Meche community living in Dhawaijan, Mechinagar, Bauhundangi, Itabhatta, and Anarmuni villages of Jhapa district. This study, based on analytical and descriptive structure, has used more qualitative than quantitative data.
british_english: This paper examines various aspects related to the marriage system prevalent in the Meche caste. The Meche community constitutes an indigenous ethnic group under the Adivasi Janajati community and represents a minority group at risk of extinction. Beyond Nepal, they also reside in certain regions of India, including Assam, West Bengal, Sikkim, and Bhutan. Within Nepal, this caste is predominantly found in diverse villages of the Jalthali region, Bhadrapur municipality, Jhapa district, such as Lakhanpur Anarmuni, Jamirmagarhi, Bauhundangi, Shanischare, Chakchaki, Bhadrapur municipality, Anarmuni, and Mahahpur Baniyani. Their distinctive social, cultural, and religious traits serve as the primary markers identifying this indigenous community. The marriage system and its various forms are also regarded as significant indicators of the caste's identity. Consequently, this study focuses on the prevalent marriage system within the Meche caste. The research encompasses the collection and analysis of both primary and secondary data and statistics. Secondary sources were gathered through literature review, while primary data were primarily obtained from Meche community members residing in Dhawaijan, Mechinagar, Bauhundangi, Itabhatta, and Anarmuni villages of Jhapa district. Employing an analytical and descriptive framework, the study prioritises qualitative data over quantitative approaches.
australian_english: This paper looks at different aspects of the marriage system found in the Meche community. The Meches are an indigenous ethnic group under the Adivasi Janajati community and are a minority group that might disappear. They live outside Nepal too, in places like Assam, West Bengal, Sikkim and Bhutan in India. In Nepal, you can mostly find them in villages around the Jalthali area in Bhadrapur municipality, Jhapa district - places like Lakhanpur Anarmuni, Jamirmagarhi, Bauhundangi, Shanischare, Chakchaki, Bhadrapur municipality, Anarmuni, and Mahahpur Baniyani. What's special about them is their unique social, cultural and religious ways of life. Their marriage system and types of marriage also tell you what kind of community they are. This paper is all about the marriage system they have. The researchers gathered information in two ways: by looking at existing sources (secondary data) and by talking directly to people from the Meche community (primary data). They did this in villages like Dhawaijan, Mechinagar, Bauhundangi, Itabhatta, and Anarmuni in Jhapa district. Their method was more about understanding the situation (qualitative) rather than just counting things (quantitative).
informal_english: This paper breaks down the marriage system in the Meche community. The Meches are an indigenous group in Nepal and they're pretty rare - almost going extinct. They also live in parts of India like Assam, West Bengal, Sikkim and Bhutan. In Nepal, you're most likely to find them in places around Jalthali in Bhadrapur municipality, Jhapa district. Those places include Lakhanpur Anarmuni, Jamirmagarhi, Bauhundangi, Shanischare, Chakchaki, Bhadrapur municipality, Anarmuni, and Mahahpur Baniyani. What makes them special is their unique social, cultural and religious identity. Their marriage system basically defines who they are as a community. This study looks closely at their marriage practices. The researchers gathered information in two ways - by looking at existing sources and by talking directly with people from the Meche community. They focused on villages like Dhawaijan, Mechinagar, Bauhundangi, Itabhatta, and Anarmuni in Jhapa district. Instead of just counting data, their approach was more about understanding the culture and society in-depth.
